tour.title: The Philosophy: CLAUDE.md
tour.description: CLAUDE.md is the behavioral contract for every Claude Code session that runs in this environment. It establishes the thin-harness/fat-skills philosophy — the harness itself stays minimal while skills provide all the domain expertise — and defines mandatory process gates in a table: brainstorm before feature work, a failing test before any implementation, worktrees before touching code, and evidence before claiming anything is done. Reading this first explains *why* every other file in this directory exists.

tour.title: The Wiring: settings.json
tour.description: Root settings.json is the nervous system that connects all three execution pipelines together. It wires nine lifecycle hooks (session-start, pre-read guard, LangSmith bundles for all eight Claude Code events), declares shell permissions, sets environment variables for LangSmith tracing, and selects the model. This single file determines what code runs and when during every Claude Code session.

tour.title: Root Lifecycle Hooks
tour.description: Three root hooks implement the core harness behaviors. The session-start hook bootstraps every session by injecting the superpowers skill pointer and the OpenWolf anatomy map so Claude always knows what files exist. The pre-read-check hook guards context efficiency by warning when a file has already been read this session. The post-compact-anatomy hook re-injects the anatomy after Claude Code compacts its context window, because compaction discards the session-start injection.

tour.title: LangSmith Plugin: Types and State
tour.description: The LangSmith plugin is a TypeScript project that traces every Claude Code session to LangSmith. Before looking at individual hooks, start with types.ts — it defines the vocabulary for the entire plugin: transcript message shapes, conversation turn structures, session state, and RunTree wrappers. Then look at state.ts, which is the most widely imported file in the project (fan-in of 17). It implements a file-backed state manager with optimistic locking so that concurrent hooks can safely share a single session state without race conditions.

tour.title: LangSmith Plugin: Transcript and Core Tracing
tour.description: transcript.ts parses Claude Code's JSONL session transcript into structured conversation turns, handling incremental reads, assistant chunk merging, tool-use/result pairing, and subagent boundary detection. langsmith.ts consumes those parsed turns and formats them into hierarchical LangSmith runs: each user prompt becomes a top-level run, each assistant response a child, and each tool call a grandchild. These two files contain the core analytical logic of the entire plugin.

tour.title: LangSmith Plugin: Hook Entry Points
tour.description: user-prompt-submit.ts and stop.ts are the two most complex hook entry points. When a user sends a prompt, user-prompt-submit.ts creates a new top-level LangSmith run and records the transcript position for incremental reading. When Claude stops, stop.ts reads the entire transcript since the last prompt, traces all turns to LangSmith, patches the top-level run with final metrics, and handles interrupted-turn recovery. Together these two hooks bookend every Claude Code turn with rich observability data.

tour.title: LangSmith Plugin: Build and Distribution
tour.description: esbuild.config.mjs compiles all nine TypeScript hook entry points into self-contained Node.js ESM bundles in the bundle/ directory. Self-contained means all dependencies are inlined — the hooks run with no npm install on target machines. hooks.json then wires all eight Claude Code lifecycle events to the compiled bundles, and this file is what settings.json at the root actually references to load the plugin.

tour.title: OpenWolf: Shared Utilities and Hook Architecture
tour.description: The OpenWolf memory system uses a different architectural pattern from the LangSmith plugin: plain JavaScript with no build step, designed for direct execution by Node. shared.js is the foundation — imported by every OpenWolf hook — and exports 14 utility functions covering wolf directory resolution, atomic JSON reads/writes, anatomy parsing, and per-line log appending. Understanding shared.js explains how all the other OpenWolf hooks communicate through a common data layer.

tour.title: OpenWolf: Pre-Write and Post-Write Guards
tour.description: pre-write.js fires before every file write and cross-references the content against cerebrum.md's Do-Not-Repeat patterns and buglog.json's known anti-patterns, emitting stderr warnings if the AI is about to repeat a known mistake. post-write.js fires after every write and updates anatomy.md with the new file description, appends an edit summary to memory.md, and auto-detects bug fixes to log to buglog.json. Together these two hooks make the AI's behavior self-correcting over time.

tour.title: OpenWolf: Persistent Memory Store
tour.description: cerebrum.md is the AI's self-learning memory: it accumulates user preferences, session learnings, do-not-repeat anti-patterns, and a decision log across every session. anatomy.md is the comprehensive file map — 520 files tracked — that gets injected at session start so Claude always knows what exists without scanning the filesystem. These two documents are what transform a stateless AI into a persistent engineering partner that improves with each session.

tour.title: Skills: The Entry Point and the Hard Gates
tour.description: The Superpowers skills library contains 15+ markdown-based skill definitions. using-superpowers/SKILL.md is the entry point — it teaches Claude how to discover and invoke all other skills and establishes instruction priority. brainstorming/SKILL.md is the first hard gate: no code may be written until a spec is designed and explicitly approved. test-driven-development/SKILL.md is the second iron law: a failing test must exist before any implementation code. These two skills enforce the process discipline that the CLAUDE.md gate table promised.

tour.title: Skills: Debugging, Verification, and SDD
tour.description: systematic-debugging/SKILL.md enforces a four-phase root-cause investigation before any fix is attempted, with an iron law against guessing. verification-before-completion/SKILL.md enforces that Claude must run and confirm verification commands before claiming work is done. subagent-driven-development/SKILL.md defines a full orchestration protocol for dispatching parallel implementer subagents, coordinating their output, and reviewing results — the most sophisticated workflow in the library.

tour.title: Skills: Session Lifecycle Skills
tour.description: Two skills are installed locally in ~/.claude/skills/ rather than in the superpowers package, which means they are always available regardless of whether superpowers is installed. wolf-init bootstraps OpenWolf in a new project from scratch. session-reflect guides Claude through two phases at the end of every session: updating cerebrum.md with learnings, then auditing CLAUDE.md for team-worthy insights that should be committed. These skills close the learning loop that makes the system self-improving.

tour.title: Superpowers: Platform Distribution
tour.description: The superpowers package distributes its skills across ten AI harnesses via platform-specific plugin manifests and a cross-platform session hook. session-start is a Bash script that reads using-superpowers/SKILL.md and emits it as a context injection — this is how skills become available at runtime. run-hook.cmd is a polyglot script (valid both as a Windows batch file and a Unix shell script) that dispatches the correct hook runner for any platform. The superpowers README documents the full installation story for each harness.
